items.title: Johor Regent decrees two-day closure of all Johor schools over haze
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: All schools in Johor will be closed tomorrow and Friday following a decree by the Regent of Johor, Tunku Mahkota Ismail, amid worsening haze and deteriorating air quality across the state. Johor Education and Information Committee chairman Dr Muhammad Naqib Md Ghazali said the closure was a precautionary measure to protect pupils' health and safety. MORE TO COME © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Ringgit ends higher against major currencies, lower versus US dollar
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit closed higher against most major currencies but lower against the US dollar on Wednesday, as the greenback strengthened broadly amid renewed concerns over Europe's fiscal outlook, an analyst said. At 6 pm, the ringgit eased to 4.0850/0895 against the greenback from Tuesday's close of 4.0835/0880. "Still, concerns over Europe's fiscal trajectory have led to a stronger US dollar.

items.title: Focus on 'civilisational harmony' over division, Anwar says
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's rich diversity, shaped over millennia by different cultures and religions, must be protected against the rise of divisive identity politics, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. He said toxic identity politics and populism driven by anti-immigration, ethnic hatred, and xenophobia are gaining traction globally and threatening democratic processes. Anwar said identity should never be used as a tool to fracture society.

items.title: AMEC seeks essential status for courier sector
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Association of Malaysian Express Carriers (AMEC) has urged the government to recognise the courier industry as essential infrastructure supporting the national digital economy and resilience in the 2027 Budget. AMEC president Ronald Tan said the budget provided an opportunity to strengthen conditions allowing courier companies to invest, improve productivity and serve businesses and consumers over the long term. Tan said the 2027 Budget should support industry modernisation through technology adoption, operational efficiency and workforce development.

items.title: Lawyer says estate administrators did not enrich themselves
items.summary: Pix Shahril Badri KUALA LUMPUR: The administrators of late Genting heiress Lim Siew Kim's RM1.6 billion estate did not enrich themselves through legal fees paid from the estate, the High Court heard. Lawyer B. Thangaraj, representing interim administrators pendente lite (APLs) Datuk S. Satharuban and Khoo Siew Kiat, said the payments were expenses incurred while carrying out their duties to preserve and protect the estate. He said Siew Kim's will stated that testamentary expenses, including legal fees, were to be paid from the estate.

items.title: Indonesia's ex-anti-graft prosecutor on trial after US$19m, 70kg gold seized
items.summary: JAKARTA: Indonesia's former top anti-graft prosecutor went on trial on money laundering charges on Wednesday, months after he was arrested with millions of dollars in cash and 70kg of gold bars found at his home and other properties. Southeast Asia's biggest economy has long struggled with corruption and has arrested scores of public officials in recent years. Febrie Adriansyah is accused of wrongdoing with public money while serving as Indonesia's top anti-corruption prosecutor.

items.title: Perak Perhilitan: Malayan tigers will only be captured if they threaten public safety
items.summary: Perak Perhilitan director Dr Pazil Abdul Patah said the assessment takes into account the tiger’s behaviour, frequency and duration of sightings, distance from residential areas, movement patterns, and evidence of interactions or attacks involving humans or livestock. “If the assessment shows a clear and continuing threat to human safety, Perhilitan will take appropriate action based on technical assessments in the field,” he told Bernama. Pazil said tiger sightings near human settlements did not necessarily mean that their forest habitat or roaming areas were shrinking, as movements could also be influenced by prey availability, habitat conditions, human disturbance, development and land use, as well as the animals’ natural movements.

items.title: MARKET PULSE PM OCT 7, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia closed lower today as concerns resurfaced over elevated oil prices and surging bond yields. Meanwhile, the ringgit fell against the greenback to 4.0860. In the crypto market, Bitcoin fell to RM342,529.

items.title: Wisma Putra to restructure to address overseas staffing shortages
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Foreign Ministry is working with several agencies to develop a restructuring plan to address staffing shortages affecting its operations, including at diplomatic missions overseas. Deputy Foreign Minister Datuk Lukanisman Awang Sauni said the ministry was working closely with the Public Service Department and the Finance Ministry on the restructuring exercise to strengthen service delivery and resolve human resource issues. He said staffing shortages at the ministry were partly due to the temporary freeze on recruitment for several public service schemes, a challenge also faced by other ministries and agencies.

items.title: Indonesia jails 35 Indian nationals over Bali online gambling ring
items.summary: DENPASAR: An Indonesian court sentenced dozens of Indian nationals to prison on Wednesday for their involvement in an online gambling operation on the resort island of Bali. Gambling is illegal in the Muslim-majority archipelago, with punishments extended to bookmakers, punters, those who promote gambling content online and gamblers themselves. The group entered Indonesia on tourist visas and had been promoting and managing transactions for an online gambling site since late last year, according to the police.

items.title: Parliament’s Palestine Caucus to submit motion on Gaza genocide for debate
items.summary: Its chairman Syed Ibrahim Syed Noh said the proposed motion would include calls for a lasting ceasefire, the protection of civilians, and safe, sustained and unhindered access to humanitarian aid. Syed Ibrahim, who is also Deputy Minister of Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability, said this at a press conference held in conjunction with the Three-Year Commemoration of the Gaza Genocide at the Parliament building here today. The Ledang Member of Parliament also said the motion would call for efforts to strengthen diplomatic action, including scrutiny of military assistance and arms transfers that risk facilitating violations of international law.

items.title: Haze: Education Ministry orders state and district education offices, schools to monitor haze, act based on API readings
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 7 — The Ministry of Education (MOE) has instructed state education departments (JPN), district education offices (PPD) and all educational institutions under its jurisdiction to continue monitoring the current haze situation in their respective locations to determine further action. It said the directive includes immediately suspending all outdoor activities, including outdoor gatherings and sports, particularly in areas with Air Pollutant Index (API) readings exceeding 100. “The haze situation has also resulted in several locations posting unhealthy API readings,” it said in a statement today.

items.title: Wan Fayhsal rushed to HKL, in stable condition
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Machang member of parliament Wan Ahmad Fayhsal Wan Ahmad Kamal was rushed to Kuala Lumpur Hospital (HKL) for emergency treatment today. His private secretary, Wan Meor Safwat Naqiuddin Shamsudin, said Wan Fayhsal had been admitted and was in stable condition. The statement did not disclose the reason for Wan Fayhsal's emergency treatment.

items.title: Khaled: LCS still operable without NSM as it has other weapons
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's Littoral Combat Ship (LCS) will still be able to operate despite not having a surface-to-surface missile as it has other weapons and combat systems. Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said the absence of the Naval Strike Missile (NSM) did not mean the LCS would be received without any weapons systems. He said the LCS would still be equipped with several other weapons systems, including surface-to-air missiles and anti-submarine warfare systems.

items.title: Witness insists Publika office existed in Hamzah Zainudin aide’s RM350,000 corruption trial
items.summary: Wan Azhar Mohamed Yusof, 51, managing director of Nexuscorpgroup Sdn Bhd (NSB), said this during cross-examination by counsel Datuk Yaacob Md Sam, appearing for Sayed Amir Muzzakkir. Yaacob: I put it to you that the handover of RM100,000 on December 4, 2020 and RM250,000 on December 16, 2020 to Sayed Amir Muzzakkir did not take place, because the said office did not exist. Wan Azhar: I disagree.

items.title: Govt seeks solution for damaged RM23.7mil Sabah housing project
items.summary: Its minister, Nga Kor Ming, said the project, completed in 2017, remained unoccupied due to structural damage caused by ground movement. "Our investigations, through the Public Works Department, found serious structural cracks in one terrace block comprising eight housing units. Although the eight affected units had been demolished, Nga said continued ground movement prevented the repair works from being completed.

items.title: Malaysia weighs missile options from South Korea, France, Turkiye for LCS
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia is considering missile systems from South Korea, France and Turkiye as alternatives to the Naval Strike Missile (NSM) for its Littoral Combat Ship (LCS) project. Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said South Korea's LIG, Turkiye's Roketsan and France's MBDA were among the suppliers being considered. He said missile purchases Malaysia had made, was making or planned to make from LIG, Roketsan and MBDA had delivery periods of around three years.

items.title: Selangor Sultan receives Silver Jubilee Keris marking 25 years on throne
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Oct 7 — Sultan of Selangor Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah today received the presentation of the Keris Jubli Perak, specially crafted to commemorate His Royal Highness’s 25th year on the Selangor throne. According to a post on the Selangor Royal Office Facebook page, the ceremonial keris was specially commissioned as an expression of Sultan Sharafuddin’s deep appreciation for the art, heritage and diverse traditions associated with the Malay keris . The Keris Jubli Perak is a symbolic work that chronicles Sultan Sharafuddin’s reign through the art of Malay heritage.

items.title: Nobel Peace Prize haunted by the 'spectre' of Trump
items.summary: DONALD Trump's chances of winning the Nobel Peace Prize are seen as minimal, but his "spectre" will cast its shadow over Friday's announcement of the winner in Oslo, experts say. Trump is "the spectre in the room", said the head of the Peace Research Institute in Oslo (PRIO), Haakon Gjerlow. He said the Nobel committee must be asking itself: "Is there any potential for this prize to create harm rather than good in awarding it?

items.title: Northern Solar secures RM34mil EPCC project
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Northern Solar Holdings Bhd, through its wholly owned subsidiary Northern Solar Sdn Bhd, has secured a RM34 million engineering, procurement, construction and commissioning (EPCC) contract for the development of a 9.50-megawatt (MW) large-scale solar photovoltaic plant. In a filing with Bursa Malaysia today, the company said the letter of award (LOA) for the project was accepted on Oct 7, 2026. It said the project is scheduled to achieve commercial operation by May 1, 2027.

items.title: LCS 1 delivery delayed again, now targeted for April 2027
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The delivery of the first Littoral Combat Ship (LCS 1) has been delayed to April 2027, four months later than the latest December 2026 target. Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said contractor Lumut Naval Shipyard Sdn Bhd (Lunas) had informed the ministry that it could no longer meet its earlier commitment to deliver LCS 1 in December. "Lunas has informed me that it cannot fulfil its previous commitment and guarantee that LCS 1 can be delivered in December 2026.

items.title: Bursa Malaysia ends lower as higher US yields, oil prices weigh on sentiment
items.summary: Among the heavyweights, Maybank slipped 10 sen to RM9.87, Public Bank slid eight sen to RM4.59, CIMB gave up 37 sen to RM7.33, Tenaga Nasional shed four sen to RM12.86, and IHH Healthcare eased one sen to RM7.90. In active trade, Top Glove fell two sen to 85.5 sen, Zetrix AI declined one sen to eight sen, V.S Industry edged down half a sen to 32.5 sen, and Supermax Corporation erased 1.5 sen to 44.5 sen, while Metronic Global was flat at half a sen. Among the top gainers, Mi Technovation jumped 38 sen to RM6.38, Batu Kawan climbed 32 sen to RM19.60, Malaysian Pacific Industries increased 24 sen to RM45.20, Petronas Dagangan rose 20 sen to RM19.32, and Gas Malaysia improved 16 sen to RM5.25.

items.title: RM1mil fund launched for intellectual property valuation
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry has allocated RM1 million for a fund to cover the cost of professional intellectual property valuation services. Its minister, Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali, said the fund was for eligible local companies to have their intellectual property assets systematically and professionally valued. "Their intangible assets involving intellectual property can therefore be officially valued to support banking financing, licensing and investment.

items.title: Perak MB tells accuser to prove allegations over special officer’s mosque speech
items.summary: IPOH, Oct 7 — Perak Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Saarani Mohamad today said that he was unsure of the veracity of an allegation that his special officer had delivered an official speech at a mosque in Kerian, stressing that the accuser must prove the claim. Saarani said the Sultan of Perak’s decree must be obeyed and that even he, despite being the chairman of state religious affairs, would not dare to deliver a speech at any mosque. “However the person making the allegation must prove it.

items.title: Hamzah ex aide's trial: Witness insists office existed for alleged money handover
items.summary: Nexuscorpgroup Sdn Bhd (NSB) managing director Wan Azhar Mohamed Yusof, 51, said this during cross-examination by counsel Datuk Yaacob Md Sam, who is representing Sayed Amir Muzzakkir Al Sayed Mohamad. Yaacob: I put it to you that the handover of RM100,000 on Dec 4, 2020 and RM250,000 on Dec 16, 2020 to Sayed Amir Muzzakkir did not take place, because the said office did not exist. Wan Azhar: I disagree.

items.title: 2027 Budget must make every ringgit count: Accountants group
items.summary: Malaysia Management Accountants Association president Dr Abdul Ahad Mohd Salleh said the fiscal deficit had narrowed from 6.4 per cent of gross domestic product (GDP) in 2021 to 3.7 per cent in 2025. On tax reform, Abdul Ahad said if the Sales and Service Tax (SST) remains, the government should examine areas where tax cascading was creating avoidable costs for businesses. On e-Invoicing, Abdul Ahad said the system should deliver benefits beyond enforcement.

items.title: Mayor of opposition stronghold Izmir defects to Erdogan party
items.summary: ANKARA: The mayor of Izmir, Turkiye's third city and an opposition stronghold, on Wednesday defected to the ruling AKP, in a huge symbolic victory for Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan. Mayor Cemil Tugay's decision to join the Islamic-rooted Justice and Development Party (AKP) was announced by Erdogan at a parliamentary group meeting in Ankara where he welcomed the mayor in a party-like atmosphere broadcast live on TV. "I welcome Izmir Mayor Cemil Tugay who is today joining the AKP family," Erdogan said as Tugay walked onto the stage and was handed a party pin.

items.title: Yinson prices US$1.46bil Agogo FPSO bonds
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Yinson Production, through its subsidiary Yinson Azalea Production Pte Ltd, has priced US$1.46 billion in bonds to refinance its Agogo floating production, storage and offloading (FPSO) vessel. Yinson said the proceeds will refinance existing debt related to the Agogo FPSO, fund required reserve accounts, pay transaction-related fees and expenses and allow for equity distributions from excess proceeds. This is the company's third FPSO project bond in three years and sets a new benchmark as the largest FPSO project bond to date.

items.title: RM8.08bil govt loan arrears manageable, says Finance Ministry
items.summary: Deputy Finance Minister Liew Chin Tong said the outstanding amount as at Dec 31 last year represented 15.67 per cent of total repayments due. As of Dec 31, outstanding loan arrears stood at RM8.084 billion, with RM5.024 billion, or 62.1 per cent, having remained unpaid for more than six years. Liew said the RM8.084 billion comprised RM5.709 billion in outstanding principal and RM2.375 billion in outstanding interest and late-payment interest.

items.title: Kosovo parliament elects new president, avoiding snap election
items.summary: PRISTINA: Kosovo's parliament elected economist Justina Shiroka Pula as the country's largely ceremonial president just before a constitutional deadline, avoiding another snap election in one of the poorest countries in Europe. Failure to elect a new president would have triggered snap parliamentary elections in the Balkan country, as it did in June. Shiroka Pula's election followed a deal between the ruling Vetevendosje party of Prime Minister Albin Kurti and opposition Democratic Party of Kosovo to limit the powers of a Kosovo war crimes court in The Hague.

items.title: MBPP disposes of more than 3,600 pest birds in September
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: The Penang Island City Council (MBPP) disposed of 3,626 pest birds in September as part of its ongoing population control efforts. The city council said the measures were aimed at maintaining cleanliness, safeguarding public health and ensuring the well-being of the urban environment. MBPP wants the public not to feed birds indiscriminately, particularly in public areas, as the practice could contribute to an increase in bird populations and create environmental cleanliness and health issues.

items.title: BN top leadership to decide on Melaka election strategy, says Zambry
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Barisan Nasional (BN) top leadership will decide whether the coalition enters an electoral pact or contests the upcoming Melaka state election on its own, said secretary-general Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abdul Kadir. Zambry said BN was aware of the nomination and polling dates announced by the Election Commission today. "Let the top leadership decide (on the electoral pact)," he told reporters after the Islam-Confucian Civilizational Cultural Festival here.

items.title: Malaysia pushes to fast-track Indonesia talks on forest fire aid as haze worsens
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 7 — Malaysia wants operational negotiations with Indonesia to be expedited to allow the country’s team to be sent to help extinguish the forest fires in that country, which have caused cross-border haze. Mohamad said he hopes that matters related to the operation can be decided quickly so that Malaysia can send a team to help their friends in Indonesia extinguish the extensive and spreading forest fires, especially in Kalimantan. Previously, the media reported that Indonesia accepted Malaysia’s offer to help extinguish the forest fires in the republic that caused prolonged haze for several weeks.

items.title: 'It's personal': Fiji minister pushes better climate finance at pre-COP
items.summary: NADI: Fiji's climate change minister wants streamlined access to financial assistance for Pacific nations, telling AFP on Wednesday the issue was "personal", with waves washing away parts of her own village. "It's frustrating at times," Tabuya said. "Some have even taken three to five years, where the access to climate finance is quite difficult."

items.title: Nhaveen murder trial adjourned to tomorrow after defence seeks time over witness statements
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Oct 7 — The High Court here today adjourned the defence proceedings of four men charged with the murder of teenager T. Nhaveen to tomorrow. The defence sought an adjournment on the ground that it required time to follow up on the delivery of four witness statements to the prosecution today. Counsel Maanveer Singh Dhillon, appearing for the four accused, informed the court that the defence had limited time to meet them in prison to prepare the said witness statements.

items.title: SMJ Fellows programme to groom Sabah's future leaders
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: The Sabah government aims to groom a generation of high-calibre leaders through the Sabah Maju Jaya (SMJ) Fellows Programme, said Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor. Hajiji said the programme was more than a youth development initiative and described it as a "nursery" for Sabah's future leadership. He said the selected fellows had the potential to lead organisations, contribute to decision-making and drive Sabah's economic development.

items.title: Govt to make viability checks mandatory for federal loans
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government plans to make viability assessments mandatory before approving new Federal Government loans, with the amount capped according to borrowers' ability to repay. Deputy Finance Minister Liew Chin Tong said the move was aimed at strengthening the government's loan assessment model and preventing the accumulation of repayment arrears. Liew said the government collected only RM465 million, or 5 per cent, of RM9.273 billion in outstanding recoverable loans in 2025.

items.title: Immediate action needed in Kuantan student's death probe, says Zambry
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abdul Kadir has called for immediate action in the investigation into the death of a 19-year-old student, who was allegedly strangled following an argument with her boyfriend. He said the incident which occurred in Kuantan was now under police investigation. "The most important thing is that immediate action needs to be taken.

items.title: Sun bear still on the loose as Perhilitan widens Seremban search
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Oct 7 — Police have stepped up patrols around Taman Tuanku Ja’afar (TTJ) after a sun bear was spotted in the residential area, with authorities widening the search as the animal remains uncaught. Negeri Sembilan Perhilitan director Wan Mat Wan Harun said the department had widened its search after the bear failed to enter a trap set nearby. Wan Mat said this was the first report the department had received of a sun bear entering the TTJ residential area.

items.title: Two senior students to face murder charge tomorrow over Kuala Pilah sports school death
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Oct 7 — Two 16-year-old boys suspected of involvement in the death of a younger boy at a sports school in Kuala Pilah last month are expected to be charged with murder tomorrow, Berita Harian reported. Negeri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said that the investigation papers had been referred to the state prosecution office. He said the prosecution had instructed that both suspects be charged with murder under Section 302 of the Penal Code, read together with Section 34, which deals with acts done by several people with a common intention.

items.title: Two corporate figures with 'Datuk Seri’, 'Datuk Wira’ titles out on MACC bail
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 7 — Two corporate figures, who are brothers holding the titles of Datuk Seri and Datuk Wira and who were previously remanded for five days to assist investigations into abuse of power and irregularities involving an investment of about RM10 million, have been released on Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) bail. According to MACC sources, the suspect with the ‘Datuk Wira’ title was released on Monday (Oct 5) after his remand period ended. “The other suspect, with the ‘Datuk Seri’ title, was released today after his remand period, which was extended by two days, ended,” the sources added.

items.title: Higher Education Ministry says institutions given autonomy to adjust learning mode when API exceeds 201
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 7 — Higher education institutions (IPTs) in areas recording Air Pollutant Index (API) readings above 201 have been given the flexibility to determine suitable teaching and learning (PdP) modes to reduce health risks while ensuring students’ education continues In a statement today, the Higher Education Ministry (MOHE) said it was closely monitoring air quality and had directed all institutions under its purview to monitor API readings in their respective areas. Bernama reported that 35 areas recorded unhealthy API readings as of 10 am today. API readings of zero to 50 indicate good air quality, 51 to 100 moderate, 101 to 200 unhealthy, 201 to 300 very unhealthy, and above 300 hazardous.

items.title: ‘I was both her mother and friend’: Zara Qairina’s mother tells inquest
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Oct 7 —The mother of the late Zara Qairina Mahathir testified at the Coroner’s Court today that she was the teenager’s principal confidante, to whom her daughter confided her troubles, joys, sorrows and matters concerning her friendships. “My relationship with Zara Qairina was indeed close. Throughout Zara Qairina’s years in primary school, Noraidah testified that she had never observed her daughter suffering any serious emotional or behavioural difficulties.

items.title: Revoked excos fight back: Ten ask High Court to void Negeri Sembilan gazette
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 7 — Ten Negeri Sembilan state executive councillors (excos) have sued the state government in the High Court to challenge the revocation of their appointments, their lawyers said today. They want the court to declare that the revocation, gazetted on September 24, is invalid. The 10 are Datuk Mohd Faizal Ramli, Datuk Zaifulbahri Idris, Datuk Mustapha Nagoor, Siow Kong Choon, Siti Nur Umairah Hashim, Datuk Mohd Asna Amin, Datuk Mohd Razi Mohd Ali, Suhaimizan Bizar, Mohd Fairuz Mohd Isa and Datuk Razali Abu Samah.

items.title: Air quality deteriorates as 37 stations enter unhealthy bracket, Klang Valley and Johor hard hit
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 7 — Air quality across Malaysia deteriorated further late this afternoon, with 37 monitoring stations nationwide recording readings in the unhealthy bracket as of 4.30pm, according to Department of Environment (DoE) surveillance data. Cheras in Kuala Lumpur followed closely behind with an API reading of 187, while Nilai in Negeri Sembilan registered 185, Putrajaya posted 183, and Batu Muda in Kuala Lumpur recorded 180. In Selangor, six stations logged elevated pollution levels.

items.title: Seven suspects: Chinese national latest held as Pahang police close in on RM1.7m Genting jewellery heist
items.summary: The man was detained after arriving at Kuala Lumpur International Airport yesterday and has been remanded until October 10 to assist police investigations, The New Straits Times reported today. “The man has been remanded until October 10 to assist investigations. “Police have so far arrested five foreigners and two locals,” Pahang acting police chief Datuk Azry Akmar Ayob was quoted as saying.

items.title: Some money in an account is linked to crime, can govt take all of it? Court of Appeal says no
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 7 — When money from an investment scam landed in a company’s bank account, the government moved to seize everything in it, but the Court of Appeal has now drawn a line on how far such confiscation can go. A three-judge panel ruled that authorities can take money proven to be linked to a crime, but cannot automatically seize the rest of the money in the same account without evidence connecting it to the offence, news outlet Free Malaysia Today ( FMT ) reported today. The prosecution was able to trace RM360,000 directly from a bank account linked to the Comoncaps investment scam into LWC’s Hong Leong Bank account, according to the FMT report.

items.title: National Unity Ministry to study effectiveness of existing 3R, hate speech laws
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 7 — The National Unity Ministry, through the Unity Issues Management Committee (JPIP), will undertake a comprehensive review of the effectiveness of existing legal provisions and enforcement mechanisms in addressing issues related to religion, royalty and race (3R), as well as hate speech. The committee will be co-chaired by National Unity Ministry secretary-general Datuk Haslina Abdul Hamid, Home Ministry secretary-general Datuk Dr Awang Alik Jeman, Communications Ministry secretary-general Datuk Abdul Halim Hamzah, and Legal Affairs Division (BHEUU) director-general at the Prime Minister’s Department Datuk Zamri Misman. “The ministry acknowledges that various legal provisions are already in place to address issues related to 3R, hate speech and social harmony.

items.title: Azalina: Follow-up action on audits generates over RM920m in government revenue
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 7 — Follow-up action on audits by the National Audit Department has contributed to revenue collection and repayments to the government amounting to RM920.91 million as at Sept 28, said Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said. She said the figure demonstrated the effectiveness of audits when identified findings were followed by appropriate action. “Audit must lead to action.

items.title: Repatriation among key issues as Myanmar president arrives in Malaysia
items.summary: SEPANG, Oct 7 — Myanmar President Min Aung Hlaing arrived in Malaysia today for a two-day official visit, with the repatriation of Myanmar nationals in Malaysia among key issues to be discussed with Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani, the minister-in-attendance, was at the airport to welcome the Myanmar leader. Also present were Malaysian Government Chief Protocol Officer Datuk Rozainor Ramli and Charge d’Affaires of Malaysia to Myanmar Johan Ariff Abdul Razak.

items.title: Tax-exempt taxpayers can opt to keep using e-invoices, says Liew
items.summary: Deputy Finance Minister Liew Chin Tong said they are part of the 1.1 million taxpayers among micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) with annual sales of RM3 million or below, who are now exempt from implementing e-Invoicing. Meanwhile, Liew said companies with annual sales exceeding RM100 million began implementing e-Invoicing on Aug 1, 2024, involving 5,578 taxpayers. He said the implementation was subsequently expanded to companies with annual sales between RM25 million and RM100 million, involving 14,567 taxpayers; companies with sales between RM5 million and RM25 million, involving 51,710 taxpayers; and companies with sales between RM3 million and RM5 million, involving 25,503 taxpayers.

items.title: Melaka state election set for Nov 14 polling, Oct 31 nomination
items.summary: MELAKA, Oct 7 — The Election Commission (EC) today announced November 14 for polling in the 16th Melaka state election, and set the nomination for Oct 31. EC chairman Datuk Seri Ramlan Harun said early voting had been set for November 10 and the campaign period would run for 14 days. Regarding the Electoral Roll (DPPR) that will be used in the 16th Melaka state election (PRN), Ramlan said that a total of 687,697 voters, consisting of 675,166 ordinary voters, 9,769 military personnel and their spouses, and 2,762 police personnel, are eligible to vote in the state election.

items.title: Disputed Undang abandon case to depose Negeri Sembilan Yamtuan, cannot refile lawsuit
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 7 — Four Undangs or traditional ruling chiefs of Negeri Sembilan — including three disputed ones — today dropped their court attempt in Kuala Lumpur to ultimately remove Yang di-Pertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir as the Negeri Sembilan ruler. Today, the four men — Datuk Mubarak Thahak, Datuk Maarof Mat Rashad, Datuk Muhammed Abdullah and Datuk Abdul Rahim Yasin — applied to the High Court in Kuala Lumpur to withdraw their court case against the Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar and the Negeri Sembilan state government. In their court case filed in July via judicial review, the four men had wanted the court to order the Menteri Besar to sign — within seven days of the court order — their April 19 declaration to “sack” Tuanku Muhriz as Negeri Sembilan ruler.

items.title: Budget 2027: Lim Guan Eng urges caution on foreign worker wage hikes over SME contract risks
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 7 — Federal lawmaker Lim Guan Eng (Bagan - DAP) today again called on the government to consider the financial impact on small and medium businesses amid rumours it could raise the minimum wage when tabling Budget 2027, warning that abrupt hikes could disrupt long-term commercial agreements. Lim, a former finance minister, argued that many enterprises operate under binding multi-year contracts where labor costs are fixed at agreed-upon rates. The former minister has been vocal in opposing the minimum wage hike and mandatory EPF contribution for foreign workers.

items.title: A bridge, fresh paint and ‘like Deepavali’: Wangsa Sari PPR in KL gets a makeover
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 7 — The park is just across Sungai Bonus, but for children at the Wangsa Sari People's Housing Programme here, getting there has meant balancing along water pipes. Resident Mohd Fazil Md Noor, 56, said it would also give children a safer and easier way to get to SK Wangsa Maju Section 1, where some currently walk or cycle. Wangsa Sari PPR resident Jasbee Kaur, 67, speaks to Malay Mail about the planned pedestrian bridge and the facelift.

items.title: Azalina sees ‘dangerous misogynistic tendency’ in violence against female students, urges closer look
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 7 — Law and Institutional Reform Minister Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said today said the recent fatal attacks on female students in schools and universities could signal a rise in misogyny, and called for the underlying causes to be examined in depth. Speaking to reporters in Parliament, she said many of the victims were women targeted by people they knew, such as classmates or faculty mates. “Young people today want everything quickly.

items.title: No warnings, just arrests: Mayor says this is how DBKL deals with parking touts
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 7 — Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) does not issue notices to parking touts and simply arrests those caught during operations, mayor Datuk Fadlun Mak Ujud said today. He said 84 touts, commonly called “ulat parking” in Malay, had been arrested in operations carried out at 49 locations around the capital. Fadlun said the operations are ongoing, but that the touts sometimes flee when enforcement officers arrive.

items.title: Malaysia’s Gen Z leads surge in support for banning children from social media, Ipsos poll finds
items.summary: The study revealed that 81 per cent of Gen Z respondents in Malaysia agree that children under the age of 14 should be barred from social media platforms both during and outside school hours, marking a sharp jump from 67 per cent recorded a year earlier. Gen X backing rose by 13 percentage points to 86 per cent, while Millennial support climbed six points to 85 per cent. Overall, 83 per cent of Malaysian adults now endorse an under-14 ban, up from 72 per cent in 2025.

items.title: Jealousy suspected in Polisas student murder; teen boyfriend remanded in Kuantan
items.summary: KUANTAN, Oct 7 — Police have recorded statements from three individuals to assist investigations into the death of a female student, who is believed to have been killed by her boyfriend at a house on Jalan Air Putih here yesterday. Kuantan District Police Chief ACP Ashari Abu Samah said police had summoned the victim’s housemates to assist investigations under Section 302 of the Penal Code. Investigations are still ongoing,” he said when contacted today.

items.title: Flying in to KLIA after midnight? Buses replace Aerotrain from 12am to 5am during software works
items.summary: SEPANG, Oct 7 — The KLIA Aerotrain will be paused from 12am to 5am during two rounds of software works in October and November, with buses taking over transfers between the Main Terminal and Satellite Building. KLIA said a full bussing service would run throughout the works as part of its operational contingency arrangements. KLIA said the update follows the Aerotrain’s completion of 20,000 continuous operational hours.
